summary: The session focuses on the importance of data products in enabling scalable and reusable data within organizations. It discusses the definition, ownership, and management of data products, emphasizing the need for dedicated roles and structured approaches to product management. Key principles include designing for scale, embedding governance, and fostering iterative development to enhance trust and usability of data products.

key_points: Data products are defined as curated, self-contained combinations of data, metadata, shared semantics, and templates.
The need for scalable and reusable data is critical for AI enablement.
Explicit accountability for data products is essential to avoid confusion over ownership.
Staffing dedicated data product managers can enhance product management.
Delivery methods include APIs, ETLs, and direct downloads to meet consumer needs.
Understanding the distinction between exchanges and marketplaces is crucial for data sharing.
Data products must be evaluated for both technical performance and user adoption.
Iterative development and feedback loops are vital for continuous improvement.

key_takeaways: Lead with product thinking to reduce rework and enhance customer-centricity.
Embed governance into the data product lifecycle to facilitate better conversations around data usage.
Design for scale by focusing on iterative development rather than one-off projects.
